crms.name: Capsule CRM
crms.blurb: The friendly CRM for small teams who never wanted a CRM that needs its own admin.

crms.name: HubSpot
crms.blurb: Powerful out of the box, expensive once you outgrow free — worth stitching to the rest of your stack properly.

crms.name: Pipedrive
crms.blurb: Sales-first, deal-pipeline thinking — made to talk to the operational tools that close the deal.

crms.name: Zoho CRM
crms.blurb: The price-conscious workhorse — ready to plug into the industry tools you already pay for.

crms.name: Copper
crms.blurb: Lives inside Google Workspace. Brilliant if you live in Gmail; useless if it doesn't reach your other systems.

crms.name: Insightly
crms.blurb: Sales plus project delivery in one place — needs proper plumbing to your accounting and ops tools.

flows.body: A prospect fills out your rate-quote form. We push the contact into {CRM}, score them against your buy box, and create the loan file in your origination system — in seconds, not hours.
When a file moves from processing to underwriting to clear-to-close, we mirror the status back to {CRM} so the loan officer and assistant always see the same picture.
Missing-doc requests fire automated emails and texts to the borrower with secure upload links — and log the chase activity against the {CRM} record.
At funding we trigger a closing-gift workflow, a 30-day check-in, an anniversary touch in year one, and a referral ask at month nine. The CRM never forgets.

A potential-client form on your website becomes a contact in {CRM}, a conflict check in your practice-management system, and — if it clears — a new matter, all without your intake person re-typing a thing.
Billable activity logged in your practice-management software shows up on the {CRM} contact record, so the partner can see at a glance which clients are warm without leaving their CRM.
Trust deposits, retainer draws, and IOLTA reconciliations flow cleanly to your accounting tool — with the rules your jurisdiction requires baked in.
When a matter closes, we update the client record in {CRM}, kick off a satisfaction survey, and add the client to a quarterly newsletter — turning a one-off into a referral source.
When a deal is marked won in {CRM}, we create the invoice in your accounting tool with the right line items, terms, and tax codes — no copy-paste, no typos.
When the client pays, the payment date and amount land on the {CRM} record so your salesperson knows the deal is truly closed — not just signed.
Overdue invoices trigger a friendly reminder to the client and a heads-up to the account owner in {CRM} — before "awkward" turns into "bad debt."
Once your books are closed for the month, the three numbers you actually care about land in your inbox — cash, AR, runway — no dashboard logins required.
When a contract is signed in {CRM}, we spin up the project workspace, create the kickoff invoice, and book the first three meetings — in one flow.
Hours logged by your team roll up to the client record in {CRM} — so a partner can see engagement health without opening four tabs.
A milestone hit in your project tool fires the invoice with the right line items and terms — retainers, progress billings, completion fees, all handled.
Sixty days before the engagement ends, {CRM} pings the partner to start the renewal conversation — with usage and outcomes summarized for them.
A signed client in {CRM} spins up the project, the Slack channel, the shared drive folder, and adds the team — from one click.
Hours logged against the client show up as a budget burn on the {CRM} record. AMs see the over-servicing risk before the month closes, not after.
When the client approves a deliverable in your project tool, the milestone invoice fires automatically and is logged back to {CRM}.
Sixty days out from retainer end, {CRM} starts the renewal conversation with the AM — with usage, deliverables shipped, and outcomes summarized.
A prospective patient books online. We create the contact in {CRM}, the appointment in your practice tool, and send the intake forms — in one stream, HIPAA-aware.
Visit notes stay in the clinical system. Visit *fact* (date, type, follow-up due) lands on the {CRM} contact so the front desk can run reminder campaigns without touching PHI.
Co-pays, self-pay charges, and insurance reimbursements flow cleanly to your accounting tool with the right service-code mapping. Your bookkeeper stops chasing you.
When a patient hits their recall window, {CRM} starts a friendly multi-channel nudge — email, text, mailed card — until they rebook.
A lead from Zillow, Realtor.com, or your IDX site lands in {CRM}, routed by zip and price band to the right agent within ninety seconds — not the next morning.
Showings booked through your platform write back to the {CRM} contact — so an agent picking up a hand-off can see exactly what the buyer has already seen.
Showings count, offer received, under contract, closed — each milestone triggers the seller communication you'd otherwise forget on a busy week.
At closing the client moves to your past-client nurture: closing gift, 30-day check-in, anniversary touch, annual property value report. The referral pipeline runs itself.
When a quote is accepted in {CRM}, we create the sales order in your ERP, kick off the production work order, and reserve the inventory — in one motion.
Low-stock and back-order events surface against the {CRM} record so your salesperson sees the supply story before the customer call — not during it.
Shipped orders trigger the tracking email to the customer and log the shipment to {CRM} — so support has the same picture sales does.
When a customer's typical reorder window hits, {CRM} pings the account owner with a suggested reorder — turning hope into a process.
A signed client requisition in {CRM} creates the open role in your ATS, the careers-page posting, and a slack-out to your recruiter team — in seconds.
Candidate movement (screen → interview → offer) updates on the client record so the account manager can run a credible status call without bothering the recruiter.
A placement fires the placement-fee invoice with the right terms (contingent, retained, guarantee window) and books the revenue to your accounting tool.
When a placement nears the end of its guarantee period, {CRM} pings the AM to start the success conversation — quietly heading off refund risk.
A booking inquiry creates the contact in {CRM} and the lead in your studio tool, sends the questionnaire, and books the discovery call — all before the client refreshes the thank-you page.
A signed contract updates the {CRM} record and triggers your onboarding workflow — welcome email, kickoff invoice, prep guide — without you opening a tab.
Milestones in your studio tool fire payment requests and write to your accounting tool — so cash flow tracks delivery, not memory.
Delivered project triggers a satisfaction note, a review request, and a referral ask at the right moment — turning happy clients into a pipeline.
A signed engagement spins up the project, the deposit invoice, and the kickoff meeting — all wired back to the {CRM} record.
Hours logged against an engagement roll up as budget health on the {CRM} record — partners spot over-servicing before it eats the margin.
A shipped deliverable triggers the milestone invoice and writes the activity to {CRM}. No "I'll bill them next week" drift.
Engagement close kicks off a satisfaction loop, a renewal conversation thirty days out, and a referral ask at month two — quietly compounding the book.
A signed project in {CRM} spins up the workspace, the task templates, the team assignments, and the kickoff meeting — from one trigger.
Project health (on track, at risk, blocked) surfaces on the {CRM} record so the account owner doesn't have to ask the PM for an update every Friday.
Each milestone fires the invoice with the right terms and writes the activity to {CRM} — so revenue tracks delivery, not memory.
On project close, {CRM} starts the next-phase conversation — with outcomes and metrics already summarized for the AM.
